festivals: Monthly special pujas on Moola nakshatra days

history.dynasty: Hoysala (12th century); later patronage by Vijayanagara and the Wodeyars of Mysore
history.period: 12th century (entrance Raja Gopura attributed to Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana)
history.summary: The Yoganarasimha Swamy Temple stands on the hilltop of the Yadugiri (Yadavagiri) hill at Melkote, overlooking the Kaveri valley - reached by some 300-450 steep stone steps (reports vary; light vehicles can go part way). Dedicated to Narasimha in a seated yoga posture, the deity is believed by legend to have been installed by Prahlada himself, and to have been worshipped by Rama, Krishna and Balarama as well as by Ramanujacharya during his 12-year stay. Built in the 12th century by the Hoysala kings (the entrance Raja Gopura by Vishnuvardhana), with later patronage from the Vijayanagara and Wodeyar kings - Krishnaraja Wodeyar III donated a gold crown - it is counted among the seven holy centres of Narasimha worship. The premises house a huge drum donated by Tipu Sultan, and the ancient stepped Kalyani tank with its mantapas nearby has featured in many Indian films.

name: Yoganarasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Melkote (Melukote) is a temple town in Pandavapura taluk of Mandya district, Karnataka, built on the rocky Yadugiri hills overlooking the Cauvery valley, about 51 km from Mysuru and 133 km from Bengaluru. It is one of the most sacred places in Karnataka, home to the Academy of Sanskrit Research with thousands of manuscripts, and a major centre of the Sri Vaishnava tradition ever since Ramanujacharya stayed here for 12 years in the early 12th century.
